tagline.text: The Philippines' only tiger safari, where you meet tigers and crocodiles in the Subic forest

location.label: Location
location.text: Ilanin Forest, Subic Bay Freeport (on the border with Morong, Bataan, administratively)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,200–2,500 (per person, estimated including transport, admission and activities)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Clark International Airport (CRK) or Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL)

children.text: Zoobic Safari is an animal theme park of about 25 hectares in the Ilanin Forest of the Subic Bay Freeport. It bills itself as the Philippines' only tiger safari, and a crocodile area, a serpentarium and a train safari follow. Families visit on a half-day trip.

Zoobic Safari is an animal park in the Ilanin Forest inside the Subic Bay Freeport. It was developed jointly with the SBMA in the early 2000s, and sources give different opening dates, from 2003 to 2004. A 2003 newspaper reported that 17 hectares of forest would be developed into an animal kingdom, a 2004 article described a safari of about 15 hectares, and later write-ups give the site as about 25 hectares. The operator at the time of development was the Yupangco group, and recent descriptions name the Zoomanity Group as the operator. The park bills itself as the "only tiger safari in the Philippines." The site is said to be a former US Navy facility turned into an animal park.

The park is divided into five main areas. There is Zoobic Park (an animal viewing and feeding area) with deer, ostriches, albino caribou and monkeys; the Savannah, where a train takes you past wild boar, potbelly pigs and ostriches; the Tiger Safari, where a customized jeepney takes you through the tiger area; Croco Loco and the Serpentarium, where you can look down on more than 200 crocodiles; and the Night Safari, held only at certain times of year. The standard tour takes about 2.5 hours and covers all the main facilities.

Based on past visit reports, the Tiger Safari is entered in a customized jeepney painted with golden tiger stripes. The windows and doors are enclosed with wire mesh, and a driver from the Aeta people was said to drive through a gate into the Ilanin forest. When a guide holds out a dressed chicken through a small window, a tiger runs up and grabs it, and there are accounts of a tiger jumping onto the roof of the vehicle. A 2008 visit report says four full-grown tigers weighing over 500 pounds (about 230 kg) were roaming the forest, most of them lying in a large pond. The way it is run now may have changed, so follow the guidance on site. Opinions differ on how to view animal welfare and safety, so decide for yourself whether to take part in contact activities (feeding and photos with tiger cubs).

This guide is for families and friends visiting Subic Bay on a day trip from Manila or Clark. Admission and extra charges change from year to year and differ between sources, and add-on activities are sometimes suspended depending on operating conditions. Ocean Adventure is next door, so many people combine them on the same day, but both take time, so we recommend splitting them over two days or going for half a day each. Be sure to check the latest rates and hours on the official website and booking platforms before you visit.

This is Zoobic Safari's signature attraction. A 2004 report described 12 adult tigers and 2 cubs in the Ilanin forest, and a 2008 visit report described Bengal and Siberian crossbred tigers. Visitors ride in a wire-meshed customized jeepney into the forest and see the tigers up close. The chicken-feeding activity costs extra (about ₱200).

An area where you can look down on about 200 crocodiles or see them at water level. The number of crocodiles is given differently by source, from more than 100 to more than 200. The serpentarium has reptiles such as pythons and boas. An activity of throwing chicken to the crocodiles also runs for a separate fee (about ₱50).
You ride a train through the park's savannah and see wild boar, potbelly pigs, ostriches and more. It is a stretch that suits children and older people who find walking hard.
An area where you can see deer, ostriches, albino caribou, monkeys and more up close. Children can also feed the animals here. Give only the food that the staff have approved.

(per a booking platform). A 2015 SBMA news item reported that a zipline passing over the tiger den had opened. Check on site whether it is running and what the height and weight limits are.

An experience of seeing the animals at night, which the park's information says is held only on Saturdays from October to January and from March to May. The schedule can change, so book ahead and confirm that it is running.

There is said to be glamping accommodation in 40-foot containers converted into animal-themed rooms. It is an option for a family to spend a night and enjoy the atmosphere after dark. Check rates and booking methods through the official channels.

Past visit reports describe passing an Aeta village on the way to Croco Loco and watching a traditional dance performance. A building converted from a former ammunition bunker is said to have housed the Animal MuZOOeum, with stuffed animals and skeletons, and a serpentarium displaying reptiles. The performances and displays may have changed, so ask for guidance when you enter.

Zoobic Safari is an outdoor park in the forest, so the dry season from November to May is easiest for walking. Days are hot with strong sun, so go in the morning just after opening.

In the rainy season showers are frequent, animals sometimes hide, and the paths are slippery. The Night Safari is said to run only on Saturdays at certain times of year, so check ahead to fit your schedule.

Subic Bay has many hotels and resorts, so it works well to stay a night and combine Ocean Adventure or the beach on the next day. The park is said to have glamping rooms in converted 40-foot containers with an animal theme. Check rates and booking methods through the official channels.
You eat at the snack stalls in the park and at nearby restaurants. Touring everything takes time, so bring water and snacks. You can also go out into Subic town for lunch.

At the reception area where you first arrive, you are said to see adult and baby tigers in large cages. Next comes Zoobic Park, where you walk a forest path and see and feed animals such as deer, ostriches, monkeys, miniature horses, goats, sheep, water buffalo and pigs close up. One report also said that at the Tigers Den you can see the caged tigers along a narrow aisle from about 60 cm away. All of this is from past visit reports, so confirm the current setup on site. One visit report said the tour was in five parts and took about 2 hours.
Going at opening time (8 AM) helps you avoid the heat and the crowds.
Rates depend on height (about 91 cm and 122 cm), so check at the entrance if you bring children.
Booking platforms require booking at least 24 hours ahead and have differing cancellation policies, so check before you buy.
Feeding and photo activities cost extra, so bring cash.
Wear comfortable shoes, a hat and sunscreen, and bring a raincoat in case of rain.
Give the animals only the food the staff have approved, and do not put your hands out.
Combining this with Ocean Adventure makes for a tight day, so pick just one if you are short of time.
A past visit report describes an itinerary that paired the park with a stay at the Subic Yacht Club and duty-free shopping at the Freeport. Pairing it with other sights in Subic makes for a full day.
Since you get close to the tiger and crocodile areas, keep children right next to a parent and follow the guides' instructions. When taking photos, do not lean on the mesh or railings.
This is a facility with tigers and crocodiles, so be sure to follow the staff's instructions. In the animal areas, do not put out your hands or any objects.
Admission and activity prices differ by source and many are dated. Check the latest rates on site.
Feeding and photo activities may be suspended depending on weather and the animals' condition.
The Night Safari and glamping may change their operating periods and booking methods, so check in advance.
When going with children, do not let go of their hands and keep them from running near the animals.
Opinions on animal welfare can be divided, so decide for yourself whether to take part in contact activities.
